statement: Under the International Entrepreneur Rule, a founder may be considered for parole by showing at least 10 percent ownership and a central and active role in a US start-up entity formed within the preceding 5 years, plus, within the preceding 18 months, a qualified investment of at least $311,071 from qualified investors or qualified government awards or grants of at least $124,429 (partial satisfaction may be supplemented by compelling evidence of growth and job-creation potential); the dollar amounts adjust every 3 years by CPI (8 CFR § 212.19(a)(1)-(2), (b)(2), (l)).
caveat: Parole is discretionary case-by-case relief, not a visa or status, and the current adjusted amounts are the ones posted by USCIS at filing time. This repo does not assess eligibility; immigration decisions need counsel.
